items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ed Kirkenby wrote in his book about 'Fats' Waller... that Don Redman was the last orchestra to play Connie's Inn, but Russell was the last band to play there.

ctx.x: I wrote to Beezie during my tour with Ralph Cooper, and when we came back to New York I went over to New Jersey to see her. And that was the start of a romance that eventually led us to start living together after I separated from Madeline. I went back into Russell's orchestra after Ralph Cooper and we played Baltimore at the Royal theater and some small towns in New York State before

being engaged to replace Don Redman in Connie's Inn. Ed Kirkenby wrote in his book about 'Fats' Waller, (Ain't Misbehavin), that Don Redman was the last orchestra to play Connie's Inn, but Russell was the last band to play there. Connie still owes me and the rest of Russel's men $200.00 in back pay.

The show was great in Connie's with Louise Cook who was a beautiful shake (1) skane-dancer, Paul Meers, one of the greatest classical dancers that New York ever knew and his second wife, 'Jazz Lips' Richardson, a comic acrobat dancer, the one and only 'Snake Hips' Tucker, The Lucky Seven Trio, three fellows who danced on big blocks made to represent dice, three girls who had a singing act, and 12 beautiful chorus girls.
